full_judgment: 65. With holding of most relevant and pertinent witnesses by the prosecution compels the court to draw adverse presumption against the prosecution under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. In a good number of authorities of Apex courts it has been laid down, particularly in the case of State vs Sarowaruddin reported in 5 BLC 451, "The prosecution has not only withheld the vital witnesses but has not also given any explanation whatsoever for their non-examination, a presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act must be drawn against the prosecution for non-examination of such material and vital witnesses."
